purpose: How a gold-plating bench turns craft into quotable services: naming service classes by the work they contain, building every price from mechanisms a quoter can re-derive (attended bench time at a costed shop rate, gold consumed from plateable area times deposit thickness times the karat and dated metal basis, drag-out and rework losses, consumables, finishing options and an explicit risk line), setting minimum charges and batch or rush adjustments as fixed-cost mechanisms, issuing written quotes whose validity window and metal-movement clause survive a moving gold price, stopping to re-quote when a job opens up, and declining work honestly when the numbers or the irreplaceability of the piece say no.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

every cost input in this KB is a shop-specific mechanism the shop measures for itself (stopwatch-timed operations, a dated metal basis from its own supplier invoices, a reconciled drag-out and rework loss factor, its own overhead bucket); no dollar figure, hourly rate, margin percentage or price level is asserted here as an industry fact

the shop sells plating work performed to a stated thickness class, never bullion ownership and never the appearance of solid gold; wear expectations are disclosed in writing before money is taken on a customer piece

commercial plating chemistry is bought and operated per the specific product's technical data sheet; bath setpoints, cycle times and deposition rates that affect cost are read from that data sheet and the shop's own logged runs, never invented here

thickness and marking ladders ('flash', 'electroplate', 'heavy', 'vermeil', 'gold filled', 'rolled gold') and karat or fineness statements are compliance classes whose numeric boundaries and entitlements are verified against the current standard and the selling jurisdiction; the in-repo testing and acceptance corpus carries that ladder as a class list and this KB only references it

all bench work priced here runs under chemical-safety obligation classes (segregation, storage, labeling, PPE, ventilation, training, emergency readiness) with the jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules verified; cyanide solutions and acids are never mixed, never stored together and never share a drain, and no price, deadline or customer pressure changes that
this KB is educational commercial reasoning, not personalized legal, tax, insurance or financial advice
exclusions: intake documentation of the customer's piece — condition photographs, the heirloom and irreplaceable-item risk acknowledgment and its signature, refusal wording and how a no is delivered, approval gates for irreversible steps, and the dispute-avoiding handover record — the sibling Client Intake & Expectation Management KB owns those artifacts; this KB consumes them and produces prices, verdicts and quotes

trade accounts and the repeat book — jeweler, retailer and repair-shop account terms, credit and payment terms, promised-turnaround commitments and reliability as a retention mechanism, courier and in-transit insurance handling for trade goods, account ledgers, job history and referral loops — the sibling Trade Accounts & the Repeat Book KB; this KB supplies the cost mechanism a trade price rests on and stops at the account relationship

how the plating is actually performed — surface preparation, bath chemistry and analysis, rack and current-distribution engineering, process execution parameters, colour control, thickness and adhesion verification methods, defect diagnosis and rework procedure — the bench specialists own those; setpoints come from the product's technical data sheet and this KB only consumes their time, metal and consumable consequences

approving regulated label or marking terms and karat or fineness claims for a finished piece — a compliance class tied to thickness and fineness thresholds in the selling jurisdiction; verify current rules before any claim, and never let a price tier name imply a marking entitlement

wear-life, durability or 'permanent finish' guarantees of any length — a quote states a thickness class and how it will be verified, and any durability statement to a customer names its measurement method or is labeled an estimate

waste, effluent and hazardous-material handling obligations — they appear here only as a real line in the overhead bucket, while the obligations themselves belong to the safety and environmental specialist and to the jurisdiction's current rules
personalized legal, tax, insurance-product or financing advice, competitor price matching as a strategy, and metal hedging or forward buying as investment activity

competency_questions.question: What does a plating quote actually own, and which decisions belong to intake, to compliance or to the trade book instead?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRICING_CHARTER states that the shop sells work performed to a stated thickness class rather than metal ownership, lists the honesty rules every quote inherits, and names the three referral lines with their receiving function

competency_questions.question: Which service class is this job — flash refresh, heavy replate, full restore or new-work plating — and what does each class include and refuse to fix?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_CLASS_TAXONOMY defines each class by its work content, prep assumption and thickness duty, and SERVICE_MENU_DESIGN shows how those classes become published tiers

competency_questions.question: What do I have to read on this specific piece before I write any number down?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PIECE_COST_DRIVERS enumerates substrate status, existing finish, stones and organics, hollow features, joints and prior repairs, surface defects and geometry, and states that the liability record itself is intake's artifact

competency_questions.question: How much gold will this job consume, and how do I get there from the piece instead of guessing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AREA_ESTIMATION gives the area methods and the interior-surface decision, THICKNESS_DUTY_SPEC ties the thickness class to the piece's duty, and GOLD_MASS_MECHANISM composes area, thickness, deposit density and karat into a re-derivable metal line

competency_questions.question: What does the gold in my tank actually cost me today, and why is the metal I buy always more than the metal that lands on the piece?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METAL_PRICE_BASIS defines a dated, sourced, shop-specific basis including the supplier premium, and METAL_LOSS_ACCOUNTING derives a reconciled loss factor from drag-out, rejects and recovery credit

competency_questions.question: How long does this job really take at the bench, and what does one hour of my shop cost to keep open?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LABOR_TIME_MODEL builds standard times per class from timed operations with attended and unattended time separated, and SHOP_RATE_OVERHEAD derives an hourly rate from a named cost bucket over realistically billable hours

competency_questions.question: How do I price the risk of harming a stone-set, repaired or heirloom piece — and when is a premium the wrong answer entirely?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RISK_PREMIUM_MODEL builds the line from likelihood factors and consequence class, states what a premium legitimately funds, and routes irreplaceable-consequence work to decline; REWORK_WARRANTY_RESERVE carries the measured return rate and the workmanship-versus-wear boundary

competency_questions.question: Why do I need a minimum charge, and how do batching and rush work legitimately change the number?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MINIMUM_CHARGE derives the floor from enumerated fixed steps at the shop rate, BATCHING_ECONOMICS states what makes a batch legitimate and what it saves, and RUSH_SURCHARGE prices expedite as displaced batch cost with a no-shortcut boundary

competency_questions.question: What must a written quote contain so that the customer and the bench read it the same way weeks later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUOTE_CONSTRUCTION lists the required sections including class and thickness duty, inclusions and exclusions, assumptions, visible price components, validity, wear disclosure, approval condition and the stop-and-re-quote clause

competency_questions.question: How long is my quote good for when the gold price moves, and what re-opens it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUOTE_VALIDITY_WINDOW sets the window from metal share and recent volatility, states the tolerance-based recompute clause, and defines the fast re-issue path; METAL_PRICE_BASIS supplies the dated figure the clause refers to

competency_questions.question: The job opened up worse than quoted — how do I re-price it without eating the loss or ambushing the customer?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_CHANGE_REQUOTE names the discovery triggers, prices the delta from the same mechanism, records it against the original quote, requires a customer decision before further work, and defines the return path if the customer declines

competency_questions.question: When is the honest answer to refuse the work, and how do I see that in the numbers rather than in my mood?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNPROFITABLE_WORK_DECLINE lists the economic thresholds (price ceiling, chronic-loser class, capability limit, process incompatibility) and the irreplaceable-consequence override, and states that the wording and delivery of the refusal belong to intake

competency_questions.question: How do I know last quarter's prices are still right, and what makes the model correct itself?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: JOB_COST_POSTMORTEM records quoted-versus-actual time, metal, options and rework per job, and PRICE_MODEL_REVIEW turns those cards into dated revisions of standard times, shop rate, loss factor and menu tiers

glossary.definition: The service class in which a thin, decorative-class gold layer is deposited over an existing sound plate with minimal preparation; the cheapest and fastest class, and the one whose wear expectation must be stated most plainly because it restores appearance rather than substance.

The service class in which the piece is stripped or thoroughly prepared, the underplate is rebuilt as the stack requires, and a wear-duty thickness of gold is deposited; costs more in both metal and attended time and carries the strongest thickness commitment.

The wetted surface that will actually receive deposit, including interior surfaces of chain links, hollow bodies and pierced work when solution reaches them; one of the two multipliers in the gold-consumed mechanism and the input most often under-estimated.

The deposit thickness class a piece's use demands — occasional-wear decorative versus constant skin-and-abrasion contact — quoted as a commitment with a verification route, never trimmed silently to hit a price.

The shop's own dated, sourced per-unit cost of the gold it buys as salts or ready-made solution, including the supplier's fabrication and handling premium over the headline spot number; the figure a quote is built against and re-derived from when the market moves.

Solution carried out of the plating tank on the work and the rack into the rinses; a real metal cost driven by withdrawal practice and part geometry, partly recoverable through rinse discipline and refiner credit and otherwise funded by the price.

The shop-specific multiplier applied to the computed deposit mass to account for drag-out, rejects, strip-and-replate and spillage net of recovery credit, derived from the shop's own purchase-versus-shipped reconciliation rather than from any published number.

The hourly cost of keeping the bench able to work — consumables, anodes, filters, water, power, waste handling fees, insurance for customer goods, rent, calibration and unbillable hours — divided by realistically billable hours, and the rate the labour line is charged at.
The stopwatch-derived time a class of job takes, broken into operations and marked attended or unattended, carried with a spread and a date so that quoting is fast and reconciliation can correct it.

The stated life of a quote together with the tolerance-based clause that recomputes the metal line at the current dated basis if gold moves before approval, converting market movement into a clerical step instead of a loss or a surprise.

nodes.definition: Fix what the pricing function owns before any number is written: the shop sells plating work — measured bench time, a stated deposit thickness over a stated area, consumables, and a documented risk position — and never sells the appearance of solid gold. The charter states the honesty rules that every downstream quote inherits: each price is built from a mechanism and a dated metal basis rather than a remembered figure; the thickness class quoted is the thickness owed; wear expectations are disclosed in writing before money is taken on a customer piece; and no job is priced that the shop would not accept losing. It also names the three referral lines that stop the quote from swallowing other people's work — intake owns condition records, the signed risk acknowledgment and the wording of a refusal; the compliance class owns regulated marking terms and karat statements, whose current rules are verified in the selling jurisdiction; and the trade book owns account terms, credit and promised turnaround.

included: ownership of the price build and the quote document
the four honesty rules every quote inherits
referral lines to intake, compliance and the trade book
the rule that the shop sells work to a thickness class, not metal ownership
excluded: condition photographs and signed risk acknowledgment
wording and delivery of a refusal
marking and karat claim approval
account credit and turnaround commitments

pros.claim: A charter stops a quote from carrying promises the bench cannot keep and the compliance class has not cleared
pros.example: an operator who wants to write '24k gold, lifetime finish' on a ring quote is redirected to the thickness class, the verification route and the wear-expectation sentence

cons.claim: The charter adds a boundary conversation to jobs that feel obvious, and a busy counter resents the ceremony
cons.example: a walk-in who wants a chain 'done today' is given a class, a scope sentence and a written figure instead of a number across the counter

failure_modes: pricing the job as if the customer were buying gold rather than buying a plating service, so every metal move becomes an argument
letting the quote make wear-life or marking claims that belong to measurement and to the compliance class
acceptance_tests: the charter states the four honesty rules, the three referral lines with their receiving function, and the sentence that the price covers work performed to a stated thickness class rather than ownership of bullion
revisit_triggers: a sibling KB boundary is redrawn and intake or the trade book absorbs or sheds a responsibility
a dispute reveals a promise the charter never bounded
the shop adds a service route (selective brush touch-up, toll-coated finishes) whose price promises are unbounded

base.update_signal: a sibling KB boundary moves, or a customer dispute exposes a promise the charter never bounded

nodes.definition: Split incoming plating work into named classes that behave differently in cost and in what they can honestly promise. A flash refresh lays a thin decorative-class layer over sound existing plate with minimal preparation: fast, cheap, and the class whose wear expectation must be spelled out because it restores appearance, not substance. A heavy replate strips or thoroughly prepares the piece, rebuilds the underplate the stack requires and deposits a wear-duty thickness. A full restore is mechanical work first — polishing out wear-through, blending, re-texturing, dealing with old solder, pitting and casting porosity — where preparation dominates the bill and the plating is almost an afterthought. New-work plating covers unworn shop-made or trade-supplied pieces with known geometry: the most predictable and most batchable class. Each class is defined by the work it contains, the preparation it assumes, the thickness duty it carries and at least one thing it explicitly does not fix, so that every quote starts from a class rather than from an impression.

included: the thickness duty each class carries
what each class explicitly does not fix
excluded: process route and bath selection
marking entitlement for a class
per-piece condition documentation
published prices for the classes

pros.claim: Named classes prevent the commonest quoting error, which is quoting a refresh and then performing a restore
pros.example: a worn-through brass-cored bangle recognised as a restore because the wear-through must be blended and the underplate rebuilt before any gold goes on

cons.claim: Classes blur at the edges and a single piece can straddle two, which invites arguing about the class instead of about the work
cons.example: a chain with sound plate along the links but bare wear at the clasp and spring ring

failure_modes: publishing price tiers with no class definitions behind them, so the tier is a number rather than a scope
defining classes by price level instead of by work content, which makes every difficult piece a negotiation
acceptance_tests: each class states its included work, its preparation assumption, its thickness duty and at least one thing it explicitly does not fix
revisit_triggers: a job type recurs that fits none of the classes
reconciled costs for one class separate into two distinct populations

base.update_signal: a recurring job type fits no class, or one class's reconciled costs split into two populations

nodes.definition: Before any estimate, read the specific piece for what will actually drive its cost. The survey covers the base metal and whether it is known or must be tested (brass, nickel silver, steel, sterling, unidentified white pot metal); the existing finish and whether it is sound, worn through or a failing old plate that must come off; stones, pearls, enamel, glue, wood, leather and other non-metallic parts that constrain chemistry, heat and handling; solder joints and prior repairs that may open in the pre-treatment chain; surface condition — pitting, deep scratches, casting porosity — that turns cheap plating into expensive metal finishing; and geometry, because recesses, chain nests and hollow shells change both the wetted area and the racking and masking time. This node is the cost read only: the liability record with condition photographs and the signed risk acknowledgment is the intake function's artifact, which this survey consumes rather than produces.

excluded: condition photography and signed risk acknowledgment
process and bath route decisions
defect root-cause diagnosis
the customer conversation about risk

pros.claim: Cost drivers found before the number is written are negotiable; the same drivers found afterwards are a loss
pros.example: spotting a soft low-melt solder repair at a pendant bail while quoting, instead of discovering it when the joint slumps in the process

cons.claim: A thorough survey spends bench minutes on every enquiry, including the many that never become jobs
cons.example: a customer who arrives with a shoebox of costume pieces and wants 'a quick price for the lot'

failure_modes: accepting the customer's claim about what the metal is instead of testing it
quoting from a phone photograph, where porosity, joints, glue and hollow construction are invisible
acceptance_tests: the survey record for the quoted piece states substrate status, finish condition, non-metallic and hollow features, joints and prior repairs, surface defects and geometry class
revisit_triggers: scope discovery recurs on one piece type, showing the survey misses a driver
a substrate identification method available to the shop changes

base.update_signal: a recurring discovery on a piece type shows the survey is missing a cost driver

nodes.definition: Estimate the plateable surface area, because area is one of the two multipliers in the gold-consumed mechanism and the one most often waved at. The bench methods are ordinary: decompose the piece into primitives and sum them (a band as a rolled rectangle, a bead as a sphere, a shank as a cylinder of wire length, a disc as two faces plus an edge); compare against a small library of previously measured reference pieces kept for exactly this purpose; use per-unit factors for repetitive items where the shop has established them by reconciliation (chain by length and style, findings by count); and for anything hollow, pierced or nested, decide explicitly whether interior surfaces will be wetted and plated, because a chain, a filigree or a hollow bead can carry several times its external silhouette. The output is an area figure carrying the method that produced it and an honest uncertainty band, not a single confident number that a fixed price then rests on.

excluded: current distribution and throwing power on the rack
thickness selection
metal pricing
masking design

pros.claim: An area with a stated method is auditable and improves with every reconciled job, unlike an intuition
pros.example: a wide cuff quoted from a decomposed area and then checked against the batch's actual metal draw, tightening the factor for the next cuff

cons.claim: Area on ornate work is genuinely uncertain, and the honest band can be wide enough to unsettle a customer
cons.example: heavily pierced filigree earrings where including the interior surfaces roughly doubles the metal line

failure_modes: using external silhouette area for chain, mesh and hollow work, so the metal line is a fraction of the truth
carrying a point estimate with no band into a fixed price and absorbing the difference
acceptance_tests: the area estimate names the method used, states whether interior surfaces are included, and carries an uncertainty band that the quote's contingency or class choice reflects
revisit_triggers: reconciliation shows one piece class is systematically under-estimated on area
racking, chain-handling or masking practice changes what gets wetted

base.update_signal: reconciled metal draw diverges from computed area on a class of pieces

nodes.definition: Decide, per job, the deposit thickness the piece's duty demands, and treat that decision as a commitment rather than a dial to trim when the price looks high. The argument runs from use: an earring back, a display piece or an item worn occasionally tolerates a thin decorative layer; a ring shank, a bracelet clasp, a watch case and anything in constant skin and abrasion contact needs a substantially heavier deposit and usually a properly rebuilt underplate to survive at all; and no thickness makes a plated piece behave like solid karat gold. Thickness is quoted as a named class, with the ladder's numeric boundaries and any marking entitlement verified against the current standard and the selling jurisdiction rather than recited from memory — the in-repo testing and acceptance corpus carries that ladder as a class list. The quoted class travels into the quote together with how it will be verified, so the customer is buying something checkable.

included: duty-to-class reasoning from how the piece is worn
the class as a quoted commitment with a verification route
excluded: numeric ladder boundaries and marking entitlement, which are verified against current jurisdiction rules
the measurement method itself
bath parameters that achieve the thickness
wear-life prediction

pros.claim: Quoting a named class with a verification route makes a higher price defensible and the outcome checkable
pros.example: a daily-worn bracelet clasp quoted at wear-duty class with an agreed verification, so the customer sees why it costs more than the refresh tier

cons.claim: Heavier classes raise both metal and attended time at once, and price-sensitive customers push back hard against the combination
cons.example: a customer who wants the price of a flash refresh with the service life of a heavy replate on a wedding band

failure_modes: quietly reducing the deposit to hit a price the customer named, which is the single most damaging dishonesty available to a plating shop
promising a wear life in months or years instead of a thickness class and a verification
acceptance_tests: the quote names the thickness class, the duty argument that justified it and how it will be verified, and contains no wear-life guarantee
revisit_triggers: warranty returns cluster on one class, suggesting its duty mapping is wrong
the referenced standard or the jurisdiction's marking rules are updated

base.update_signal: returns cluster on a duty class, or the referenced thickness and marking standard is revised

nodes.definition: Establish what the gold in the tank actually costs this shop, and date it. The basis is not the headline spot number: plating salts and ready-made solutions arrive from a supplier at spot plus a fabrication and handling premium, billed in the supplier's units — gold content per litre of made-up solution, or grams of gold per unit of salt — so the shop's true per-gram cost is what it paid on the last replenishment plus the premium it will pay on the next. In practice the shop records one basis figure with its unit, its source document and its date, quotes against it, and treats movement beyond a stated tolerance as the trigger to refresh the basis and re-price open quotes. The basis is deliberately shop-specific and time-stamped; repeating someone else's number as if it were a universal price is precisely the error this node exists to prevent.

included: what to record as the basis: unit, source document, date
the shop-specific nature of the figure
excluded: metal trading, hedging or forward buying
any assertion of a universal or industry price
bath analysis of actual gold concentration
customer-facing metal price commentary

pros.claim: A dated basis makes every quote reproducible and gives the validity window something concrete to refer to
pros.example: re-issuing a two-week-old quote by swapping one dated figure instead of rebuilding the whole estimate

cons.claim: Keeping a live basis is administrative work a busy bench postpones until a loss teaches it otherwise
cons.example: a shop still quoting from an invoice three replenishments old while the supplier premium has moved twice

failure_modes: quoting from headline spot and absorbing the supplier premium invisibly on every job
treating the basis as a promise made to the customer rather than as one input that the movement clause is allowed to refresh
acceptance_tests: the recorded basis names its unit, its source document, its date, and the movement tolerance that forces a refresh
revisit_triggers: the metal price moves beyond the stated tolerance
the supplier changes its premium, its billing unit or its solution concentration

base.update_signal: a replenishment invoice or supplier quotation lands with a different premium, unit or concentration

nodes.definition: Build the metal line from the mechanism rather than from a feeling: the gold laid down is a volume — plateable area multiplied by deposit thickness — converted to mass through the deposit's density, then to money through the fine-gold fraction implied by the deposit's karat or alloy and the dated metal basis. Every link in that chain is a lever the quoter must feel in the hand: doubling the thickness class doubles the metal; a piece with twice the area costs twice the metal at the same class; an alloyed or hardened deposit carries proportionally less fine gold per unit of volume than a fine-gold deposit, which changes the money but not the wear argument; and the mass that lands on the piece is never the mass that leaves the tank. The line is written with its inputs visible — area and its method, thickness class, karat basis, dated metal basis — so it can be re-derived in seconds when any one of them moves.

included: the volume to mass to fine-gold-content to cost chain
the direction and size of each lever
showing the inputs on the quoted line
excluded: bath make-up, replenishment chemistry and cathode efficiency tuning
the loss and recovery accounting
sourcing the price basis
deposit hardness and colour engineering

pros.claim: A derived metal line survives a challenge and can be re-quoted immediately when gold or scope moves
pros.example: a trade customer asking why the wear-duty class costs more per piece receives the area-times-thickness argument rather than an apology

cons.claim: The mechanism's apparent precision is limited by its weakest input, usually area, so it can manufacture false confidence
cons.example: a carefully computed metal line resting on a filigree area estimate that ignored the interior surfaces

failure_modes: pricing metal from the piece's own weight, which is substrate and tells you nothing about the deposit
ignoring that an alloyed deposit changes the fine-gold content per unit volume, so the karat basis silently drifts out of the line
acceptance_tests: the metal line shows area with its method, thickness class, karat basis and metal basis date, and recomputes correctly when any single input is changed
revisit_triggers: the shop changes the deposit alloy or karat it offers
reconciled metal draws diverge persistently from the computed deposit mass on a class

base.update_signal: the offered deposit alloy changes, or reconciled draws stop matching the computed mass

nodes.definition: Account for the gap between metal bought and metal delivered on customers' pieces, because that gap is a real cost that either sits in the price or comes out of the margin. The mechanisms are well known on a bench: drag-out carries solution out of the tank on the work and the rack into the rinses, and cups, blind holes, chain nests and rough surfaces carry more of it; bath depletion is settled by replenishment invoices that are the true metal spend; rejects and strip-and-replate consume the metal twice; filtration changes, spills and contaminated racks lose it outright; and recovery — disciplined drag-out rinses and returning spent solutions and rinse concentrates to a refiner — puts some of it back as a credit. The product of this node is a shop-specific loss factor derived from its own purchase-versus-shipped reconciliation over a stated period and applied per class in the quote build, never an invented industry allowance.

included: the loss mechanisms and what makes each worse
refiner recovery credit as an offset
deriving the loss factor from reconciliation
excluded: waste treatment, effluent and hazardous-material obligations, which belong to the safety and environmental specialist and to jurisdiction rules
bath maintenance procedure
refining chemistry and refiner contract terms

pros.claim: An explicit loss factor stops a shop from slowly funding its customers' gold out of its own pocket
pros.example: a quarter in which replenishment invoices clearly exceeded the metal billed across all jobs, traced to drag-out on chain work with poor withdrawal practice

cons.claim: The factor is only as good as the reconciliation behind it and is noisy at low job volume
cons.example: one heavy restore distorting a slow month's factor badly enough to mislead the next quarter's pricing

failure_modes: pricing only the metal that lands on the piece and treating everything else as an unexplained shrinkage
booking refiner credit as profit rather than as the offset the price already assumed
acceptance_tests: the loss factor traces to a named reconciliation period comparing metal purchased against metal computed as delivered, and is applied per class in the quote build
revisit_triggers: reconciliation drifts outside its historical band
racking, withdrawal or rinse practice changes
a new geometry class such as deep-cup or heavy chain work enters the mix

base.update_signal: a purchase-versus-shipped reconciliation lands outside the factor's historical band

nodes.definition: Price time from timed work, not from impression. Break a job into the operations that actually consume bench minutes — receiving and marking the piece, disassembly and stone protection or removal, mechanical preparation such as polishing and wear-through blending, cleaning and activation handling, masking and racking, the plating cycles with their rinses, drying, post-finishing, inspection, re-assembly, packing, and the administrative minutes of quoting and record-keeping — and time them with a stopwatch across real jobs until each class carries a standard time with a spread. Two truths dominate the model and surprise every new shop: preparation and finishing usually swamp the time spent in the tank, and it is attended time that costs money while unattended cycle time can overlap other work if the bench is organised to exploit it. Standard times are held per class and per complexity band, dated, and corrected from reconciliation rather than copied from another shop.

included: stopwatch-derived standard times with spread and date
times held per class and complexity band
excluded: process step content and its parameters
turnaround promises to trade customers
labour law, payroll and staffing advice
individual operator performance management

pros.claim: Standard times make quoting fast and consistent and expose which classes are quietly unprofitable
pros.example: discovering that 'quick' flash refreshes on chain consume nearly as much attended time as a new-work batch several times their value

cons.claim: Timing work is disliked at the bench and the resulting standards go stale as technique and equipment change
cons.example: a new ultrasonic and better racking cutting real preparation time while the model still bills the old figure

failure_modes: billing unattended tank time as though someone were standing over it, which prices the shop out of its own market
forgetting the recurring minutes of quoting, handling, inspection and packing that every job pays regardless of size
acceptance_tests: each service class carries a standard time built from timed operations, each marked attended or unattended, with a spread and the date it was measured
revisit_triggers: equipment or technique changes materially
reconciliation shows systematic time overrun or underrun on a class

base.update_signal: reconciled attended minutes diverge from the standard time for a class, or the shop re-equips

nodes.definition: Convert the cost of the shop simply existing into an hourly rate the labour line can charge, instead of pretending consumables are free. The bucket is long and every item is real: anodes and their consumption, filters and pump maintenance, buffs, wheels, compounds and abrasives, masking materials, deionised water and rinse turnover, rectifier and heater power, tank heat-up energy where the process needs it, PPE and the running cost of ventilation, chemical waste collection and handling fees, calibration and test consumables, insurance covering customers' goods on the premises, rent, utilities, and the unbillable hours the bench spends quoting, cleaning, maintaining tanks and chasing suppliers. Divided by the hours that can realistically be billed in a period — never by total open hours — the result is a rate per attended hour with a stated basis and a review date, alongside a short list of genuinely job-specific consumables billed separately when they are big enough to matter.

included: the rate's stated basis and review date
excluded: bookkeeping, tax and financing advice
safety equipment specification and its obligations
waste disposal procedure and legal duties
premises and lease decisions

pros.claim: An honest rate stops the shop from selling hours for less than an hour costs to provide
pros.example: seeing that waste collection fees, rinse water and anode consumption alone eat a visible share of every assumed billable hour

cons.claim: The billable-hours denominator is the hardest honest number in a small shop and a generous guess silently under-recovers everything above it
cons.example: assuming most of the working day is billable in a shop that actually spends much of it on enquiries, tank care and collections

failure_modes: using total open hours as the denominator, which understates the rate by a large factor
leaving waste fees, insurance on customer goods or unbillable time out of the bucket entirely
acceptance_tests: the rate states its cost bucket, its billable-hour denominator, the period it was computed from, and the cadence on which it is recomputed
revisit_triggers: a step change in utilities, waste fees, insurance or rent
realised billable hours diverge from the assumed denominator

base.update_signal: a utility, waste, insurance or rent cost steps materially, or realised billable hours differ from the denominator

nodes.definition: Price the risk a specific piece carries as an explicit line built from two factors, and recognise the region where no premium is honest. The first factor is how likely this piece is to be harmed by the work: stones that will not tolerate the heat or the chemistry, glued settings, pearls and organics, brittle old solder, thin worn shells that may perforate during preparation, unidentified pot metal, and pieces that must be disassembled to be plated at all. The second is what the consequence of harm would be: an ordinary replaceable costume item, a valued but replaceable piece, or something sentimentally irreplaceable. A premium legitimately funds the extra care a difficult but replaceable piece needs — slower handling, protective masking, an inconspicuous test area, additional inspection. It cannot buy back a grandmother's ring. As consequence approaches irreplaceable, the correct output of this node is not a larger number but a decline or a referral, with the documented risk acknowledgment itself handled at intake.

included: likelihood factors read from the piece
the irreplaceable cut-off that routes to decline
excluded: the signed risk acknowledgment and the intake conversation
insurance policy selection and claims handling
damage diagnosis after the fact
any assurance that a premium makes an outcome safe

pros.claim: Separating the risk line makes it discussable and reviewable instead of hidden inside a mysteriously padded price
pros.example: a stone-set vintage ring quoted with the masking, slower handling and extra inspection shown as what the line buys

cons.claim: An explicit premium can read to a customer as the shop admitting it might break the piece
cons.example: a customer who hears the risk line as a confession and takes the job to a shop that says nothing at all

failure_modes: using a premium as self-granted permission to accept a job that should have been declined
applying one flat premium to every customer piece regardless of what it actually carries, which prices the easy work out and the dangerous work in
acceptance_tests: the risk line names the likelihood factors observed on this piece, its consequence class, and what the premium funds; work in the irreplaceable consequence class is routed to the decline path instead of being priced
revisit_triggers: a realised damage event or a near miss
a new piece type enters the mix whose failure modes are unmapped

base.update_signal: a damage event or near miss occurs, or a piece type arrives whose failure modes are not in the likelihood list

nodes.definition: Carry the cost of the work that comes back inside the price, and draw the line between what the shop owes and what it does not. Some fraction of jobs will be redone: a colour that does not match the customer's other pieces, a missed spot in a recess the rack shadowed, an adhesion failure traced to preparation, a piece the shop's own inspection stops before it ships. Measured from the shop's own returns log per class, that fraction becomes a reserve inside the class price instead of an occasional morale-destroying loss. The warranty boundary is written in the same breath and printed in the quote: defects of workmanship within a stated period are the shop's to put right; ordinary wear-through of a deposit that was plated to the agreed class, impact damage, chemical exposure by the wearer and third-party alteration are not. The boundary is only defensible because the thickness class and the wear disclosure were recorded at quote time.

included: measured rework fraction per class as a reserve
the boundary's dependence on the recorded class and disclosure
excluded: defect root-cause diagnosis and the rework procedure
intake handover records that evidence condition
statutory consumer-warranty interpretation, which must be verified in the selling jurisdiction

pros.claim: A measured reserve turns returns from an emergency into a line item and reveals classes that cannot be sold profitably at all
pros.example: a refresh tier whose return rate quietly consumed its entire contribution until the returns log made it visible

cons.claim: Reserves raise the visible price of good jobs to pay for the bad ones, which loses quotes to shops that ignore the problem
cons.example: losing a trade enquiry to a competitor whose price assumes nothing ever comes back

failure_modes: keeping no returns log, so the reserve is a feeling that moves with the last bad week
offering a warranty promise wider than the quoted thickness class can physically support
acceptance_tests: the class price carries a reserve traceable to a returns log, and the quote states the workmanship-versus-wear boundary next to the quoted thickness class
revisit_triggers: the return rate on a class moves outside its historical band
a warranty dispute exposes ambiguous boundary wording

base.update_signal: the measured return rate for a class leaves its historical band, or a dispute exposes unclear boundary wording

nodes.definition: Price the work that surrounds the deposit as named options rather than absorbing it silently. The list is the shop's own capability list: mechanical finishing beyond what the class assumes (deep scratch removal, wear-through blending, re-texturing a satin, brushed or bead-blast surface to match the rest of a piece), selective or masked two-tone work, post-plate treatments the shop actually offers where the product's data sheet supports them, disassembly and re-assembly, restringing, engraving-safe handling, ultrasonic cleaning of the finished piece, and the packaging and return handling the piece needs. Each option carries its own attended time, its own consumables and its own honesty note — most importantly that a protective topcoat is a wear aid rather than a thickness substitute, and can never be sold as making a plated piece permanent. Named options turn an argument about a total into a customer's choice about scope.

included: named pre- and post-plate options with their own time and consumable basis
masking and two-tone work as an option
excluded: the topcoat product's process parameters and cure schedule, which come from its data sheet
durability claims of any kind
marking or label wording
jewellery repair work the shop does not perform

pros.claim: Options convert a fight about price into a decision about scope that the customer controls
pros.example: a customer who declines full scratch removal on a bangle and accepts the surface as-is, with that choice written on the quote

cons.claim: An option list lengthens the quote and can confuse a customer who wanted a single number
cons.example: a walk-in facing four separate line items for one pair of earrings and losing confidence in the shop

failure_modes: absorbing hours of scratch removal inside a refresh price because it felt awkward to itemise
selling a protective topcoat as a durability guarantee rather than as a wear aid
acceptance_tests: each offered option carries its own attended time and consumable basis, and any topcoat option is described as a wear aid with no permanence or wear-life claim attached
revisit_triggers: the shop gains or drops a finishing capability
a topcoat or treatment product's data sheet changes what may honestly be said about it

base.update_signal: the shop's finishing capability list changes or a product data sheet alters what may be claimed

nodes.definition: Set a minimum charge, because a large part of every job's cost does not scale with the size of the piece: receiving it and marking it against a ticket, examining and recording it, quoting, racking and masking, running tanks and rinses that cost the same whether they hold one earring back or forty, inspecting, packing, and the administration of returning it. Below a certain job size the honest price for those fixed steps is larger than a customer expects, and the shop has to choose its response deliberately — hold the minimum and explain it as setup, or offer a batched small-item route that trades a longer wait for a shared setup. The figure itself is derived, not chosen: the enumerated fixed steps at the current shop rate plus the smallest realistic metal and consumable draw. It is reviewed whenever the rate is recomputed and published on the menu so that nobody meets it for the first time at the counter.

included: the batched small-item alternative as the honest concession
review coupled to the shop rate
excluded: trade-account volume pricing and account terms
relationship discounting policy
per-job risk pricing
loss-leader marketing decisions

pros.claim: A stated minimum stops the shop losing money on friendly favours that each consume a whole setup
pros.example: a single earring post that occupies the same receive, rack, run, inspect and pack chain as a full bracelet

cons.claim: A minimum turns away small jobs that would have brought the customer back with large ones
cons.example: a regular customer's tiny repair sent to a competitor, and the next heavy replate going with it

failure_modes: publishing a minimum that does not actually cover one setup, so small work is subsidised invisibly
waiving the minimum case by case until it no longer means anything and the menu is fiction
acceptance_tests: the minimum is derived from the enumerated fixed steps at the current shop rate plus a minimum materials draw, and it appears on the published menu
revisit_triggers: the shop rate is recomputed
small-job volume changes materially in either direction

base.update_signal: the shop rate is recomputed or the mix of small jobs shifts materially

nodes.definition: Treat batching as the shop's principal cost lever and price it deliberately. Running like work together — same class, same thickness duty, compatible substrates and a shared pre-treatment chain — spreads tank warm-up where the process calls for it, rack preparation, solution handling and inspection setup across many pieces at once, and it lets attended preparation on one job overlap unattended cycle time on another. The mechanism has hard boundaries: a batch is legitimate only when the pieces genuinely share process requirements, incompatible substrates or pre-treatment chains must never be forced together to save an hour, and the customer's promised date has to survive the batch window. Pricing follows the mechanism honestly: a batched route really is cheaper per piece and may be offered at a lower price with a longer window, while a piece that must run alone carries the whole setup and should be priced as such rather than subsidised.

included: the amortised cost lever and what it actually saves
the window as the customer-visible cost of batching
excluded: rack design and current-distribution engineering
promised turnaround as a trade retention mechanism
scheduling software and shop-floor sequencing tools
process compatibility rulings, which belong to the bench specialists

pros.claim: Batching is the difference between a viable small shop and one that loses money on every solo run
pros.example: holding trade new-work pieces of one class until the rack is properly loaded instead of running a half-empty tank per incoming order

cons.claim: Batching pushes lead times out and tempts an operator to force incompatible work into one run
cons.example: a substrate whose pre-treatment chain differs being slipped into a full rack to avoid a second setup

failure_modes: batching by convenience rather than by shared process requirement, which converts a saved hour into a scrapped rack
promising a date the batch window was never going to meet
acceptance_tests: each batch records the shared class, thickness duty and pre-treatment chain that make it legitimate, and each batched quote states the window it assumes
revisit_triggers: the throughput mix changes so that batches no longer fill
a substrate or finish class arrives that cannot join any existing batch

base.update_signal: batch fill rates change, or a new substrate class cannot join existing runs

nodes.definition: Price expedited work as the measurable cost of interrupting the shop's own economics, not as a penalty and not as a favour. A rush displaces a batch: it may force a solo run whose setup is amortised over a single piece, push other customers' promised dates back, consume attended hours at an inconvenient time, and raise the probability of an error made in a hurry. The surcharge is assembled from those components and quoted alongside what the customer actually receives for it — a specific date, not merely urgency. The boundary is absolute and stated in the same sentence: a rush buys position in the queue, never shortcuts. Preparation chains, rinses, process cycle times, cure or dry steps and inspection are not compressed to make a date, and any request that can only be met by truncating them is refused with the reason given rather than accepted as a private gamble.

included: what the surcharge buys, which is position and a date
the displacement of other jobs as a real cost
excluded: the shop's standing turnaround policy for trade accounts
process cycle-time parameters themselves
courier and delivery arrangements
penalty clauses and service-level contracts

pros.claim: A mechanism-based rush price makes urgency a priced choice instead of a favour that quietly wrecks the schedule
pros.example: a wedding-week clasp replate run solo at an itemised surcharge while the standing trade batch keeps its promised date

cons.claim: Rush work fragments the week and, once habitual, turns a batching shop into a solo-run shop still charging batch prices
cons.example: three small favours in one week that leave the main batch under-loaded and the month's margin gone

failure_modes: accepting a date that can only be met by shortening a preparation, rinse, cycle or inspection step
charging the rush but silently absorbing the delay imposed on the batch's other customers
acceptance_tests: the surcharge is itemised against displaced batch setup and attended hours, and the accepted date is demonstrably achievable without shortening any process or inspection step
revisit_triggers: rush frequency rises to the point of reshaping the schedule
a class's process cycle time changes what dates are feasible

base.update_signal: rush requests change in frequency, or a process cycle time changes which dates can be honoured

nodes.definition: Package the classes, the minimum and the options into a small published menu that a customer can understand and the bench can actually execute, with the honesty built into the names rather than bolted on in small print. A workable menu names each tier by the work it contains instead of by adjectives — a refresh tier, a standard replate tier, a wear-duty tier, a restoration tier priced only after assessment, and a new-work or trade tier priced per batch — and states for each what is included, what the thickness duty is, what is excluded, and which minimum applies. It carries the wear-expectation sentence in plain reading language, and it marks clearly which tiers can be quoted from a published figure and which are only ever quoted after the piece has been seen. The menu is simultaneously a marketing artifact and a discipline artifact: anything not on it must be quoted from the cost build, and anything on it must have been costed from that same build.

included: tier definitions with inclusions and exclusions
excluded: any wording implying a tier is solid gold or carries a marking entitlement, which is a compliance matter to verify in the jurisdiction
trade price lists and account terms
advertising durability claims
competitor price comparison tables

pros.claim: A menu shortens the quoting conversation and pre-answers the questions that otherwise become disputes after collection
pros.example: a customer choosing the wear-duty tier for a daily-worn ring after reading exactly what the refresh tier does not do

cons.claim: Published tiers invite comparison on price alone and go stale as costs move underneath them
cons.example: a printed price list left on the counter through a substantial metal-price move and several supplier increases

failure_modes: publishing tiers that were never costed from the build, so the menu and the mechanism disagree on every difficult job
naming a tier in a way that implies permanence, solid gold or a marking entitlement the piece does not have
acceptance_tests: every published tier traces to a cost build, states its thickness duty and exclusions, and carries the wear-expectation sentence; no tier name implies solid gold, permanence or a marking entitlement
revisit_triggers: the price model review changes a tier's cost basis
a tier's realised margin diverges from the intended band
guidance on regulated marking terms changes in the selling jurisdiction

base.update_signal: a model review revises a tier's cost basis, or a tier's realised margin leaves the intended band

nodes.definition: Assemble the priced job into a written quote that the customer and the bench will read the same way weeks later. Its anatomy is fixed: identification of the piece with a reference to the condition record produced at intake; the service class and the thickness duty; what is included and, explicitly, what is not — stone tightening, structural repair, dent removal, matching another piece's colour, resizing; the assumptions the price rests on, such as substrate as tested or merely as stated by the customer, the area basis used and whether disassembly is required; the price with its components visible enough to be defended — attended time at the shop rate, metal from the mechanism with its basis date, the loss factor, consumables, chosen options, and the risk line where one applies; the validity period; the wear-expectation and never-solid-gold sentence; the approval and deposit condition; and the stop-and-re-quote clause. This document is simultaneously the shop's main honesty instrument and its main defence in a dispute.

excluded: intake condition photographs and the signed acknowledgment, which are referenced rather than reproduced
payment terms and credit for accounts
contract and consumer-law positions, which must be verified in the jurisdiction
delivery and courier arrangements

pros.claim: A complete written quote settles most disputes before they exist, because it says plainly what was and was not bought
pros.example: a customer expecting a dent removed reads the exclusion line at quote time and either adds the option or accepts the piece as it is

cons.claim: Writing a full quote costs real minutes per enquiry and feels bureaucratic on a two-piece refresh
cons.example: a small counter job that takes about as long to document properly as it takes to plate

failure_modes: giving a verbal number with no scope, exclusions or validity and discovering the difference at collection
hiding the composition of the price so thoroughly that no challenge can be answered without inventing something
acceptance_tests: the issued quote contains piece identification, class and thickness duty, inclusions and exclusions, stated assumptions, priced components, validity period, wear disclosure, approval condition and the stop-and-re-quote clause
revisit_triggers: a dispute exposes a missing or ambiguous clause
the menu or the cost model changes what must be stated on the document

base.update_signal: a dispute or a model change reveals a clause the standard quote does not carry

nodes.definition: Give every quote an explicit life and a stated rule for what happens when the gold price moves inside it or after it. The mechanism has three parts. First, a validity period chosen against how volatile the metal basis has recently been and how much of this particular price is metal at all — a labour-dominated restoration can safely hold a longer window than a heavy replate on a large-area piece. Second, a movement clause stating that if the basis moves beyond a named tolerance before approval, the metal line is recomputed at the current dated basis while attended time, options and the risk line stand unchanged. Third, a re-issue path for expired quotes that swaps in the new basis instead of rebuilding the estimate from scratch. Written this way, a moving market becomes a clerical event rather than either a loss the shop silently absorbs or a surprise the customer experiences as bad faith.

included: choosing the window from metal share and recent volatility
the customer-facing explanation of why a window exists
excluded: hedging, forward buying or any financial-instrument advice
the basis figure itself and its sourcing
trade price-list refresh cycles for accounts
speculating about future metal prices for a customer

pros.claim: An explicit window protects both sides and removes the temptation to pad every price against imagined movement
pros.example: a large-area heavy replate quoted with a short window and a written recompute rule instead of an invisible cushion nobody can justify

cons.claim: Short windows irritate customers who want time to think, while long windows on metal-heavy jobs transfer real exposure onto the shop
cons.example: a customer returning a month later with the same piece, the same quote in hand and a different metal basis in the market

failure_modes: issuing quotes with no window at all and then honouring stale ones at a loss to avoid an argument
writing a movement clause so vague that it reads as licence to re-price arbitrarily
acceptance_tests: every issued quote states its validity period, the metal basis date it rests on, and the tolerance and recompute rule that applies if the basis moves
revisit_triggers: the metal volatility regime changes enough to make current windows wrong
customers dispute re-priced quotes, indicating the clause is unclear

base.update_signal: metal volatility changes materially, or a customer dispute shows the movement clause is read differently by both sides

nodes.definition: Handle the job that turns out to be a different job. Discovery is routine in plating: the old plate lifts and reveals pitting the finish was hiding; the supposedly silver chain proves to be plated base metal; a solder joint opens in the pre-treatment chain; a stone loosens or clouds and must come out; the interior of a hollow piece proves to carry several times the area estimated. The rule is to stop at the discovery, price the delta from the same mechanism that produced the original quote — added attended hours, added area or thickness need, a changed risk position, additional consumables — and obtain the customer's decision before proceeding. The approval gate for irreversible steps and the wording of that conversation belong to intake; the commercial change order belongs here. The change is recorded against the original quote so the final invoice reconciles line by line, and if the customer declines, the piece is returned in its documented state with only the authorised work charged.

included: the discovery triggers a quoter should expect
delta pricing from the same mechanism
the change recorded against the original quote
the decline-to-proceed path and what may be charged
excluded: the approval-gate wording and signed authorisation for irreversible steps
the technical remedy for the discovery itself
refunds and consumer-law positions, which must be verified in the jurisdiction
renegotiating account terms

pros.claim: Stopping to re-quote turns what would have been a loss or a dispute into an ordinary transaction
pros.example: pitting revealed under an old plate on a bangle, priced as added preparation hours and accepted in writing before any further work

cons.claim: Stopping costs schedule time and can strand a partly processed piece while the customer is unreachable
cons.example: a piece already stripped to bare substrate waiting days on a decision, occupying rack space and needing protective handling meanwhile

failure_modes: absorbing discovered work silently, which either destroys the margin or quietly shortens the process to compensate
continuing past an irreversible step without the authorisation intake requires
acceptance_tests: every scope change is recorded as a delta against the original quote with its own mechanism-derived price and a recorded customer decision before further work proceeds
revisit_triggers: one discovery type recurs often enough that it belongs in the cost-driver survey
a stranded-piece incident exposes a gap in the hold-and-protect procedure

base.update_signal: a discovery type recurs across jobs, or a stranded-piece episode exposes a procedural gap

nodes.definition: Decide from the numbers and the risk position, rather than from mood or fatigue, when the right answer is no. The economic tests are explicit: the mechanism-built price exceeds what the piece is worth or what the customer will pay, and cannot be reduced without thinning the deposit or skipping preparation; the job belongs to a class the reconciliation shows is a chronic loser that no batching or process change fixes; the piece needs work the shop does not do well, such as structural repair, stone setting or complex disassembly, and buying that in destroys what is left of the margin; or the substrate and construction simply cannot take the process. Above all of them sits the risk override: where the consequence of loss is irreplaceable, the job is declined regardless of the price offered. This node produces the verdict and hands it over — the conversation, the referral to a better-suited shop and the way the refusal is delivered belong to intake.

included: the chronic-loser class test from reconciliation
capability limits stated as an economic fact
excluded: how the refusal is worded and delivered to the client
the intake refusal-criteria list itself
referral relationships and who receives the work
any legal duty to serve, which must be verified in the jurisdiction

pros.claim: Predefined thresholds make a refusal defensible and unemotional, and they protect the shop from the one job it would never stop remembering
pros.example: a thin worn-through gold-filled locket where the honest verdict is that plating cannot restore metal that is no longer there

cons.claim: Declining costs revenue today and can send the customer to a shop willing to attempt what should not be attempted
cons.example: an irreplaceable ring refused here and accepted elsewhere by someone who never mentions the risk at all

failure_modes: accepting a chronic-loser class because activity feels like business
substituting a larger risk premium for the decline that an irreplaceable piece required
acceptance_tests: each decline records which threshold fired — price ceiling, chronic-loser class, capability limit, process incompatibility, or irreplaceable consequence — and the verdict is handed to intake for delivery
revisit_triggers: a class is repeatedly declined yet keeps arriving, suggesting a service gap worth designing for
the shop's capability changes what it can honestly accept

base.update_signal: a declined class keeps arriving, or the shop gains a capability that changes what it can accept

nodes.definition: Close every job by comparing what was quoted against what it actually consumed: attended minutes by operation against the standard time, metal drawn — from replenishment allocated across the batch and the computed deposit — against the metal line, consumables and options used, rework performed, and the final invoice against the original quote plus any recorded changes. The record is deliberately short, because a heavy form is a form nobody fills in: a job card carrying class, attended time, area basis, thickness class, metal basis date, quoted and actual figures, and one line on whatever surprised the operator. Its value is cumulative rather than immediate. After a few dozen cards the shop knows which classes it prices correctly, which piece types it consistently under-times, whether its loss factor is real, and which customers' work costs more than it looked like it would.

included: quoted versus actual on time, metal, consumables and rework
keeping the record light enough to survive a busy week
excluded: financial accounting, payroll and tax treatment
the customer-facing account ledger and job history that build the trade book
defect analysis and root-cause work
operator performance appraisal

pros.claim: Reconciliation is the only mechanism that makes the whole price model self-correcting instead of self-confirming
pros.example: discovering that restoration jobs consistently overran on polishing time, which no amount of quoting instinct had ever revealed

cons.claim: It is post-job administration at the least motivated moment, and partial data can bias the model worse than no data
cons.example: only the painful jobs getting cards, which makes an otherwise sound class look unprofitable

failure_modes: recording revenue but not consumption, so the cards cannot correct anything
letting the card grow long enough that it is skipped on exactly the busy weeks that matter most
acceptance_tests: each closed job has a card with quoted versus actual attended time, the metal basis and computed metal, options used, rework performed, and a reconciliation of the final invoice
revisit_triggers: card completion rate drops below the level that makes the sample trustworthy
a new service class enters the mix with no card format for it

base.update_signal: card completion falls, or the accumulated cards contradict a standard time or the loss factor

nodes.definition: Recalibrate the whole model on a stated cadence and on named triggers, rather than when a bad quarter finally makes it obvious. The review reads the accumulated job cards and asks a fixed set of questions: are the standard times still right for each class after equipment and technique changes; is the shop rate still covering its bucket after utility, waste-fee, insurance and rent movement; is the loss factor consistent with the latest purchase-versus-shipped reconciliation; has the metal basis moved far enough to re-price the published menu and shorten validity windows; is any tier running at a margin the shop would not knowingly choose to sell; and does the minimum still cover one real setup. The outputs are explicit and dated: revised standard times, a revised rate, a revised loss factor, republished menu tiers with an effective date, and a short note of what changed and why, so that every quote issued afterwards is traceable to a version of the model.

included: the review cadence and its trigger list
traceability from an issued quote to a model version
excluded: business strategy, financing and tax planning
competitor price matching as a policy
trade-account negotiation and volume agreements
wage and staffing decisions

pros.claim: Versioned, dated outputs let the shop explain why this month's price differs from last month's without inventing a story
pros.example: showing a trade customer that the menu's effective date changed alongside a recorded metal basis and shop rate revision

cons.claim: A review cadence is easy to skip in a busy season, and republishing prices carries its own customer-relations cost
cons.example: deferring the review through a strong quarter and quoting all of it on stale standard times and an old rate

failure_modes: reviewing prices without reviewing the cost inputs underneath them, which is guessing with extra steps
changing published prices with no effective date, so old quotes and new tiers collide at the counter
acceptance_tests: each review produces dated revisions of standard times, shop rate, loss factor and menu tiers with a change note, and issued quotes reference the model version in force
revisit_triggers: the cadence is missed
any input steps materially between reviews
a tier's realised margin falls outside its intended band

base.update_signal: a scheduled review lands, or an input steps materially enough to trigger one early

edges.why_related: classes are defined inside the charter's rule that the shop sells work to a thickness class rather than metal ownership
the survey is the cost read the charter authorises, with the liability record left to intake
each class carries a thickness duty, so the class must be named before the duty can be argued
geometry, hollow features and construction found in the survey determine which area method applies and whether interiors count
the survey's findings on finish condition, stones, joints and porosity select the complexity band whose standard time applies
area is the first multiplier in the metal mechanism and carries its uncertainty into it
the quoted thickness class is the second multiplier and scales the metal line linearly
the dated per-unit basis converts computed deposit mass into money
the loss factor is applied to the computed deposit mass to reach metal actually purchased
the likelihood factors in the risk line are exactly the hazards the survey records on the piece
the reserve extends the risk view from damage during the job to work that returns after it
the minimum is the enumerated fixed steps at their standard times, so those times must exist first
batching saves the setup operations the time model isolated, and needs the attended-versus-unattended split to quantify the saving
the expedite price is the measured cost of breaking the batch economics
the menu must publish where the minimum applies, so the floor has to be derived before tiers are printed
a quote either instantiates a published tier or builds from the same model the tiers were costed from
the metal line and its visible inputs are a required component of the quote document
the window and movement clause are clauses of the quote and inherit its metal basis date
a change order is priced as a delta against the original quote and its stated assumptions
the decline verdict is read off the assembled price against the piece's value and the risk position
the card reconciles actual consumption against the components the quote made visible
the review has nothing to read without the accumulated job cards
the charter's honesty rules bound what a quote may say: no solid-gold representation, a wear-expectation sentence, and a thickness class rather than a wear-life promise
the rule that no job is priced which the shop would not accept losing sets the outer bound on what may be quoted at all
the recent volatility and the age of the basis constrain how long a window may honestly be offered
no published tier may promise a duty its thickness class cannot carry, which bounds how tiers are named and described
accepting expedited work breaks the batch that the shop's whole cost structure depends on, and the surcharge rarely covers the disruption to other customers' dates
edges.resolution_rule: accept a rush only when the itemised surcharge covers the displaced setup and attended hours AND the batch's other promised dates still hold; if the date can only be met by shortening a preparation, rinse, cycle or inspection step, refuse the date and say why — process integrity and safety obligations outrank the fee

edges.why_related: the minimum repels exactly the small jobs a published menu is designed to attract, and waiving it quietly makes the menu untrue
edges.resolution_rule: hold the minimum and publish it, then offer the small-item route as a named tier that trades a longer batch window for a shared setup; never waive the floor silently on a case-by-case basis

edges.why_related: a premium can be made to look as though it prices any risk, which lets a shop talk itself into a job it should refuse
edges.resolution_rule: the decline verdict dominates whenever the consequence class is irreplaceable or the loss would be uninsurable: a premium may fund extra care on replaceable pieces only, and no fee converts an irreplaceable piece into an acceptable risk

edges.why_related: a published menu implies price stability while the metal basis underneath it keeps moving
edges.resolution_rule: print an effective date and a stated metal-basis review trigger on the menu, and let the per-job quote with its own window govern whenever the two disagree

edges.why_related: counter pressure for an immediate number fights the survey depth a defensible quote requires
edges.resolution_rule: give a class-level indication clearly labelled as an indication and not a quote, and issue a firm written price only after the survey; never convert an indication into a commitment by repeating it

edges.why_related: under-specifying thickness for the piece's duty causes early wear-through and the warranty traffic the reserve has to absorb
an unaccounted or drifting loss factor makes the metal line under-recover, which is one of the signals that forces a model revision
the class is named first and the piece is then surveyed for the drivers that matter within that class
when a job is approved late, the expiry and metal-movement check runs before any scope delta is priced onto it
actual attended minutes per operation retune the standard times and their spreads
realised damage, near misses and rework events recalibrate the likelihood factors and consequence classes
the review republishes tiers with a new effective date when rate, times, loss factor or metal basis have moved
both are mechanisms that recover a fixed, non-scaling cost that per-piece pricing would otherwise hide, and both are explained to the customer as setup rather than as a penalty

conflict_axes.name: thickness_owed_versus_price_ceiling
conflict_axes.description: The deposit thickness the piece's duty demands collides with what the customer is willing to pay, and the cheapest way to close the gap is the one that must never be taken.
poles: deposit the thickness the duty demands
hit the price the customer named
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never thin the deposit silently; re-scope to a lower class with its wear expectation stated plainly in writing, or decline the job

conflict_axes.name: batch_window_versus_promised_date
conflict_axes.description: Batching is the shop's main cost lever and it needs waiting time, while customers and trade accounts want their goods back quickly.
poles: hold work until the batch is legitimate and full
run now to meet the date
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: quote the batched route with its window as the standard offer and price a solo or expedited run at its true displaced cost; never force incompatible work into one rack to save a setup

conflict_axes.name: counter_speed_versus_survey_depth
conflict_axes.description: A customer standing at the counter wants a number now, while the survey that makes a number honest takes bench minutes.
poles: answer immediately
survey before committing
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: offer a class-level indication explicitly labelled as an indication, and issue the firm written quote only after the piece has been read

conflict_axes.name: risk_premium_versus_honest_refusal
conflict_axes.description: Difficult pieces can be priced for extra care, but pricing implies acceptance, and some consequences cannot be bought back at any price.
poles: price the risk and take the work
refuse the work whatever the fee
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: premium only where the piece is replaceable and the documented acknowledgment exists; as consequence approaches irreplaceable the decline verdict dominates absolutely

conflict_axes.name: menu_simplicity_versus_job_specific_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: Customers want a small comprehensible price list while real pieces differ enough that only a per-job build is accurate.
poles: publish simple flat tiers
quote every job from the cost build
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: publish tiers only where the cost build is genuinely stable, and mark restoration and unusual work as assessment-only rather than inventing a flat figure for it

conflict_axes.name: quote_life_versus_metal_exposure
conflict_axes.description: A long validity window is a courtesy to the customer and an open position on the metal price for the shop.
poles: give a generous validity period
keep exposure to metal movement short
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set the window from the metal share of the specific price and recent volatility, and carry a tolerance-based recompute clause instead of padding every quote

conflict_axes.name: minimum_charge_versus_relationship_goodwill
conflict_axes.description: The floor that keeps small work from being subsidised is the same floor that turns away the tiny favour a good customer remembers.
poles: hold the published minimum
waive it for the relationship
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the published floor and offer the batched small-item route as the concession, so the goodwill is real and the economics stay true

conflict_axes.name: throughput_pressure_versus_safety_and_process_integrity
conflict_axes.description: Money and deadlines push toward shortened preparation, skipped rinses, crowded racks and hurried chemical handling.
poles: hit the margin and the date
keep every process and safety obligation intact
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: safety and compliance obligations and full process cycles outrank price, throughput and deadline without exception; if the number only works with a shortcut, the number is wrong and the job is re-quoted or declined

conflict_axes.name: price_transparency_versus_commercial_confidentiality
conflict_axes.description: Showing the price components makes a quote defensible and also exposes the shop's cost structure to customers and competitors.
poles: show the full component breakdown
quote a single defended total
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: show component categories and the mechanism behind them — attended time, metal from area and thickness at a dated basis, options, risk — without publishing the underlying rate, loss factor or supplier terms

conflict_axes.name: absorbing_rework_versus_charging_it
conflict_axes.description: Redoing work at the shop's own cost protects the relationship, while charging it protects the margin, and the line between workmanship and ordinary wear is where the argument lives.
poles: absorb the return to keep the customer
charge it as wear or damage
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide by the written boundary and the recorded thickness class rather than by the mood of the conversation, and price a reserve so genuine workmanship returns are already funded

edge_cases.description: A customer's 'gold' bracelet turns out to be a base-metal core whose old plating hid deep pitting, so the quoted refresh is actually hours of metal finishing
edge_cases.trigger: the existing finish conceals substrate damage that only appears once the old plate lifts
edge_cases.mitigation: survey for porosity and wear-through before quoting, quote the refresh with an explicit assumption that the substrate is sound, and stop at the discovery to price the delta as added preparation before proceeding

edge_cases.description: The gold basis moves sharply between issuing a quote and the customer approving it weeks later
